value.body: A two-year master's degree covering organic, inorganic, physical and analytical chemistry, with lab work and often a project. Many universities let students specialise in one branch in the second year. It leads to industry lab roles, research and teaching.

items.label: PG students in Chemistry
items.note: Based on institutions that reported data

items.label: Main entrances
items.note: JAM for IITs, IISc and some NITs; CUET-PG for many central and state universities

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc with chemistry (usually with minimum marks set by each university). Admission is through IIT JAM (Chemistry), CUET-PG, or a state or university entrance test.

value.title: At a glance
items: Pharma, chemicals and testing labs hire M.Sc chemists for QC, analytical and production roles.
CSIR-NET or GATE opens funded Ph.D. positions and research careers.
School and college teaching need further qualifications (B.Ed, or NET/SET/Ph.D.).

value.title: Postgraduate students in Chemistry
value.note: Subject-level PG enrolment in Chemistry (mostly M.Sc). AISHE counts responding institutions only; coverage varies by year.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 13 (PG level), actual responses (Ministry of Education)
